title: Ship the Lore pane mod in the opum-lore plugin (OPAG-1075)
description:
Operator decision OPAG-1075, relayed by opum-doc as ODOC-OP-2026-10-02-11; operator chose "A: dispatch to lore-cli (Recommended)". lore-cli builds the mod in the opum-lore plugin, releases it, and opum-marketplace moves the pin.

WHAT. A Claude Code hooks module (a "mod") shipped in the opum-lore plugin from this repository: a Lore pane that views documents (raw and rendered markdown), searches, edits and creates. Design brief: opum-doc `docs/reference/lore-mod-design-brief.md`, read by ref at main e62e764 on 2026-10-02. opum-marketplace's opum-lore entry pins opum-ai/lore-cli at v0.12.0 (read by ref 2026-10-02); after this release exists, opum-agent dispatches the pin move.

PLATFORM. Mods need Claude Code 2.1.287 or later; the fleet runs the frozen 2.1.287 pair.

SIBLING. quest-cli's Quest board mod (QCLI-431, draft opum-ai/quest-cli#481) is the pattern mirrored here: plugin-root hooks/, types/, tests/; scripts/mod-test.mjs stages exactly the shipped files and runs `claude plugin validate --strict` + `claude plugin test`; CI gates those two while tsc is machine-local, because the engine writes its declaration only for a session-loaded mod. The id-collision defect their prototype showed (a pane creating records in a checkout colliding with records created on branches) has a create-path counterpart here: the pane's New surface writes a file into the working tree, so it must not offer id allocation that ignores refs.

OPERATOR QUESTIONS, none decided (route to opum-agent as A/Bs when reached; never decide locally; never ask in-pane): (1) body editing — external editor vs in-pane editor vs Claude-assisted only; (2) fleet view — reading other repositories' bundles through a Lore workspace manifest (opum-family currently fails to load because one member does not validate); (3) one mod or two — separate mods per plugin (current direction) vs one Opum workspace pane hosting both.

LIMITS. The release and any registry publication are tier 3, through this session's own dialog. No restart or rollout of the session (OPAG-1069 holds).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The opum-lore plugin ships a hooks module registered from hooks/hooks.json; `claude plugin validate --strict` passes against a stage of exactly the plugin's shipped files, and the module registers a lore command that opens the pane.

Browse and Read: the pane lists the repository bundle's concepts from `lore query` and opens one rendered as Markdown from `lore read`; internal link clicks navigate in the pane with a working Back; a Raw toggle shows the source file including frontmatter.
Search: free text with type and tag filters runs `lore query` and opens results in Read; the include-open-PRs toggle uses `--across-refs`.
New: creates a document through `lore new` from the `lore types` vocabulary with title, summary and tags, and opens the result showing the type's required sections.

Edit, in the session's own repository only: the fields form rewrites frontmatter then validates the written file with `lore validate`, surfacing Lore's own message and keeping the previous file when validation fails; structural operations (rename, supersede, task link/unlink) run the matching lore command and then `lore sync`.
Body editing ships the arm the operator selects when Q1 is routed to opum-agent before implementation, covered by the module's tests.

scripts/mod-test.mjs stages the plugin's shipped files, runs `claude plugin validate --strict` and `claude plugin test`, and reports the typecheck state honestly (machine-local tsc against the engine's declaration; NOT TYPECHECKED rather than implied-green when none exists); CI runs it on PRs.

The operator's answered design questions are recorded through lore as ADRs under this task, their answers verbatim once relayed; the module's own design choices are recorded in a Reference doc and on this record; `lore check` exits 0 and `bun test` passes on the landing branch.

The release carrying the module is tagged and published through the repository's normal release path (tier 3, via this session's own dialog), after the Q3 A/B is relayed and answered; opum-agent is then told so the marketplace pin move can be dispatched.

definitionOfDone.text: Reviewer pass on hooks/, scripts/mod-test.mjs and .github/workflows/ci.yml before landing (repository rule: anything touching scripts/ or CI gets a reviewer pass).
All gates green with evidence: biome lint, typecheck, bun test, lore check, mod validate + test.
No unaddressed reviewer findings at landing.

3. Core surfaces: Browse, Read (rendered/raw, link navigation, Back), Search (filters, across-refs), New — driven only by lore CLI stdout, per the brief's recommendations.

4. Route operator questions as A/Bs when reached: Q1 (body editing) before the edit surface, Q2 (fleet view) before the scope chrome, Q3 (one mod or two) before the release — Q3 stays open and is the operator's (orchestrator correction 2026-10-02). Implement the chosen arms.
5. Edit surface: fields form + lore validate; structural ops via lore commands + lore sync; uncommitted-changes strip with the prompt-fill landing path.
6. Contract + tests: types/index.d.ts for $.state; engine tests (claude-code/testing) per surface under tests/.
7. Wiring: scripts/mod-test.mjs (staged validate + test; machine-local tsc), package.json test:mod and tests/** exclusion, tsconfig excludes, a ci.yml job.
8. Docs: operator answers recorded verbatim as ADRs under this task once relayed; this task's own design choices in a Reference doc and on this record; lore check + bun test green.
9. Land: reviewer pass, PR to dev, merge after required gates.
10. Release via tier-3 dialog only after the Q3 A/B is relayed and answered; report to opum-agent for the marketplace pin move.
implementationNotes: Orchestrator review, 2026-10-02 (relayed while building; plan approved): (1) ADRs only for decisions the operator actually makes — their answers verbatim, once relayed, under this task; my own design choices go in a Reference doc and on this record, not ADRs. (2) Q3 (one mod or two) stays open and is the operator's: send as an A/B before the release, so a published shape does not settle it by default — not only when shared code appears. (3) AC8 and plan steps 4/8/10 updated accordingly; Q1/Q2 A/B timing (before each surface is implemented) confirmed correct.

First slice landed on the work branch at f71bed1c (1952 lines): hooks/hooks.json, hooks/register.tsx, hooks/lore.ts, types/index.d.ts, tests/pane.test.tsx, tests/lore.test.ts. Gates re-run against a stage of exactly the shipped files: `claude plugin validate --strict` exit 0 (engine inventory: hooks session.start, command.run{command=lore-pane}, ui.render{Pane}; calls process.run, fs.read, fs.write, prompt.fill, command.register, clock.every, ui.open, ui.panes, ui.resolve; state keys view/catalog/doc/edits), `claude plugin test` 12/12 pass, tsc against the 2.1.287 engine declaration exit 0. Test coverage: browse+open+Back+Raw toggle; search submit, --across-refs --allow-partial, type filter; fields save through lore validate; failed validation restores the previous file and shows lore's own message; new through lore new then opens the result; rename + lore sync argv; link press navigates in-pane.

Structural constraint discovered (now recorded in the module's own comments): the engine's validator refuses `$` or any noun of `$` passed across an import -- every `$.noun` call lives in register.tsx; hooks/lore.ts takes plain values only (an argv to run, a run's result).

Decisions this session made (its own, not the operator's; a Reference doc entry to follow): the module is built in the repo layout from the start rather than a dev-mods hot-reload copy, so there is one canonical source and the same staged validate/test/tsc loop runs locally and in CI. hooks/, types/ and tests/ stay outside biome.json's include list, mirroring quest-cli's shape; formatting was applied with a throwaway config in repo style, and the wiring slice records the coverage answer in the tsconfig covenant comments.

It is honest where the module is not yet whole: body editing currently ships the fields form + Claude-assisted revision (Q1 unanswered), and ConceptDoc.links is declared but never populated in v1 (no lore graph call) — populate it or drop it from the contract when the side strip lands.

EVIDENCE, as measured (re-run, do not quote): `node scripts/mod-test.mjs` exit 0 — 13/13 engine tests, validate passed, tsc clean against the bundled 2.1.287 declaration. `bun run typecheck` exit 0. `bun run lint` exit 0 (11 pre-existing warnings, none naming these files). `bun run lore check` exit 0 (86 files). `bun test` 4920 pass / 1 skip / 1 fail — the single red is test/link-quest-race.test.ts, the KNOWN LCLI-645 workstation-only case (skipped in CI), re-verified as pre-existing by the documenter running it solo and from a clean HEAD archive. `git ls-tree v0.12.0 hooks/` returns nothing: no tagged release carries the pane yet.

TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS a successor must not relearn:
- The engine validator refuses `$` or any noun of `$` passed across an import. Every `$.noun` call lives in hooks/register.tsx; hooks/lore.ts takes plain values (an argv, a run's result). The validator names each cross-boundary function when it refuses.
- `lore read` reports `path` relative to the BUNDLE (adr/x.md); `lore validate` and `$.fs` address repository-relative paths. repoPathFor() (hooks/lore.ts) applies the docs/ prefix once; ConceptDoc carries repoPath. The bug was caught by probing the real CLI envelope — the mocked tests returned raw bytes whatever path was asked for, so the browse test now captures the fs.read path and pins /repo/docs/adr/0001-x.md (commit 5e9c8ab4). Also: the engine test kit settles work a handler left unawaited, but state writes are async — handlers that act on what they just wrote must await it first (the submitWith and submitActionWith shapes; a read-before-write race bit twice).
